correctness.rationale: Three disjoint descendant weights are counted respectively by bounded three-gap compositions, an exact union of two one-marker position intervals, and a unique all-zero descendant. Double counting source/descendant pairs yields the all-radius mean, including boundary values. Coefficientwise gap balancing plus discrete threshold convexity yields the finite optimum; three independent deleted-gap allocations characterize saturation. A Python checker independently enumerated 3,003 distinct-subsequence sets and checked 1,101,870 finite maximum/plateau cases. Finite checks corroborate but do not prove the universal identities.

value.rationale: For sparse constant-composition sources, precise distinct deletion-output counts govern the diversity of a deletion channel. The theorem supplies both exact arbitrary-radius mean over all weight-two inputs and an all-extremizer saturation threshold, revealing that for fixed deletion radius almost every long weight-two word reaches the maximum bounded descendant diversity. It is an infinite exact fixed-composition structure and distribution not merely an arbitrary small numerical slice.
